scope.note: Compact provenance and assay-scope index. Authored interpretations are not independent experimental evidence; raw primary retrievals and full audit inventories remain in the temporary research packet.

primary_sources.scope: Human fetal/postnatal kidney and mouse development studies establish renal membrane and segmental distribution. Fetal human staining is less polarized; detailed mouse apical observations are not relabeled as human experiments.
primary_sources.access: Selected original institutional full PDF Methods and Results were read; the protected normal abstract remains unchanged.

primary_sources.scope: Purified human C-terminal domains directly bind ATP, ADP and AMP and show weak self-association. Nucleotide-binding-site mutations change currents in an uncoupled E211A background, whereas wild-type-background currents remain unchanged.
primary_sources.access: Actual publisher article, corrected Figure 4 and supplementary material were recovered. The owner read selected Results/Methods text; the independent consultation additionally inspected figure pixels and the correction. The normal abstract remains unchanged.
primary_sources.construct_scope: Human isolated C-terminal domain. Methods says 568–746, Results says 571–746 in historical 746-residue numbering; no exact mapping to either current product is asserted. Corrected Figure4d labels used by the independent consultation.

primary_sources.scope: Official Table 1 positively detects human placental ClC5 with seven peptides, but its adjusted enrichment P value is 1. Detection and significant lysosomal enrichment are distinct conclusions.
primary_sources.access: Actual official indexed Table 1, Methods and footnotes were recovered independently. Supplementary peptide PDFs remained blocked; the protected abstract cache is unchanged.

primary_sources.scope: Human ClC-5 tail and KIF3B constructs associate in multiple assays. KIF3B affects surface abundance and uptake differently in HEK293 and polarized opossum kidney cells; ClC-5 is not assigned kinesin motor activity.
primary_sources.access: Selected Methods and Results from the full normal cache were read, with exact interaction records examined separately.

primary_sources.scope: The authentic abstract describes YTS-cell membrane proteomics, but the exact ClC-5 target result and peptides remain inaccessible.
primary_sources.access: Only the complete authentic abstract was accessible; the exact target table was not recovered.

primary_sources.scope: The complete abstract connects human CLCN5 variants with renal disorders and reduced oocyte currents. It does not independently establish proton coupling or provide the unrecovered full assay details.
primary_sources.access: Only the complete authentic abstract was accessible; a repository route returned an access challenge.

primary_sources.scope: ClC-5-dependent proton flux, gradient tests and uncoupling mutants distinguish exchange from passive chloride conduction. The original stoichiometry estimate is rough rather than a precise universal cycle count.
primary_sources.access: The authentic author-hosted original PDF supplies direct exchange evidence; selected ClC-5 Results/controls were read, with the full four-page study independently assessed in the earlier consultation. The normal abstract remains unchanged.

primary_sources.scope: Mouse E211A knock-in uncouples chloride conduction from proton exchange. Renal endocytic defects persist despite normal bulk ATP-driven vesicle acidification, separating coupled exchange from a simple shunt-conductance model.
primary_sources.access: Selected original article and supplementary Methods were read from authentic institutional PDFs; the normal abstract remains unchanged.

primary_sources.scope: Human ClC-5 expressed in HEK293 cells contributes a bafilomycin-insensitive vesicular acidification component, with transport mutants as controls. Separate opossum-cell knockdown and a proposed proton-entry model are kept at their assay scope.
primary_sources.access: Selected actual full PMC Methods and Results were read; the normal abstract remains unchanged.

primary_sources.scope: Human ClC-5 constructs in oocytes support direct chloride/proton transport measurements; epithelial-cell localization distinguishes wild-type endosomal/surface pools from mutant retention. Apparent stoichiometry is calculated from transport energetics.
primary_sources.access: Selected actual full normal Methods and Results were read.

primary_sources.scope: TMEM9-family partners associate with and regulate human ClC-5 in heterologous systems, while mouse renal experiments distinguish TMEM9B-dependent transporter stability. Tagged constructs and other CLC-family controls are not treated as interchangeable.
primary_sources.access: Selected actual full normal Methods and Results were read with human-transporter, mouse-partner and tissue distinctions.

binding.scope: Six exact records comprise two yeast two-hybrid records, one pull-down, two reciprocal anti-tag co-immunoprecipitations and one confocal colocalization. Five are association assays; the sixth is not a binding assay. Human CLCN5 tail numbering in the literal records is 621–816, whereas the paper uses 551–746 historical numbering. The exact records and construct labels are retained without claiming current product identity solely from length. KIF3B is the kinesin motor partner; ClC-5 is not assigned its ATPase or motor activity. No self-pair was returned for PMID:17195847, but direct primary sedimentation independently supports that original assertion.

propagation.scope: Current records distinguish experimental grounding from repeated propagation. Historical PAINT trees, MSAs and IBD placement were not reconstructed. Target self-inclusion is legitimate experimental grounding, and donor number is not an evidential-strength score. Curated is_active_in relations are retained and are not silently replaced by located_in.

localization.scope: Official supported main locations are Golgi apparatus and plasma membrane, with cytosol as an additional location. CACO-2 and RH-30 show Golgi/plasma membrane; U-2 OS shows plasma membrane/cytosol. Selected actual images were viewed; these do not replace native renal compartment evidence.

reactome.scope: The target is an alternative catalyst-set member, not a transported substrate or an obligatory CLCN4/5/6 complex. The modeled exchange consumes endosomal chloride and cytosolic proton and produces the opposite pools; actual flux direction remains gradient- and context-dependent.

terms.label: membrane
terms.definition: A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.

terms.label: renal system process
terms.definition: An organ system process carried out by any of the organs or tissues of the renal system. The renal system maintains fluid balance, and contributes to electrolyte balance, acid/base balance, and disposal of nitrogenous waste products. In humans, the renal system comprises a pair of kidneys, a pair of ureters, urinary bladder, urethra, sphincter muscle and associated blood vessels; in other species, the renal system may comprise related structures (e.g., nephrocytes and malpighian tubules in Drosophila).

terms.label: voltage-gated chloride channel activity
terms.definition: Enables the transmembrane transfer of a chloride ion by a voltage-gated channel. A voltage-gated channel is a channel whose open state is dependent on the voltage across the membrane in which it is embedded.

terms.label: chloride channel activity
terms.definition: Enables the energy-independent facilitated diffusion of a chloride ion through a transmembrane aqueous pore or channel.

terms.label: lysosomal membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding the lysosome and separating its contents from the cell cytoplasm.

terms.label: cytoplasm
terms.definition: The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.

terms.label: Golgi apparatus
terms.definition: A membrane-bound cytoplasmic organelle of the endomembrane system that further processes the core oligosaccharides (e.g. N-glycans) added to proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum and packages them into membrane-bound vesicles. The Golgi apparatus operates at the intersection of the secretory, lysosomal, and endocytic pathways.

terms.label: chloride transmembrane transporter activity
terms.definition: Enables the transfer of chloride ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

terms.label: endosome
terms.definition: A vacuole to which materials ingested by endocytosis are delivered.

terms.label: plasma membrane
terms.definition: The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.

terms.label: identical protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to an identical protein or proteins.

terms.label: antiporter activity
terms.definition: Enables the active transport of a solute across a membrane by a mechanism whereby two or more species are transported in opposite directions in a tightly coupled process not directly linked to a form of energy other than chemiosmotic energy. The reaction is: solute A(out) + solute B(in) = solute A(in) + solute B(out).

terms.label: protein binding
terms.definition: Binding to a protein.

terms.label: ATP binding
terms.definition: Binding to ATP, adenosine 5'-triphosphate, a universally important coenzyme and enzyme regulator.

terms.label: chloride transport
terms.definition: The directed movement of chloride into, out of or within a cell, or between cells, by means of some agent such as a transporter or pore.

terms.label: ADP binding
terms.definition: Binding to ADP, adenosine 5'-diphosphate.

terms.label: Golgi membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments of the Golgi apparatus.

terms.label: apical part of cell
terms.definition: The region of a polarized cell that forms a tip or is distal to a base. For example, in a polarized epithelial cell, the apical region has an exposed surface and lies opposite to the basal lamina that separates the epithelium from other tissue.

terms.label: chloride:proton antiporter activity
terms.definition: Enables the transfer of a solute or solutes from one side of a membrane to the other according to the reaction: chloride(out) + proton(in) = chloride(in) + proton(out).

terms.label: endosome membrane
terms.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding an endosome.

terms.label: monoatomic ion transmembrane transport
terms.definition: A process in which a monoatomic ion is transported across a membrane. Monatomic ions (also called simple ions) are ions consisting of exactly one atom.

terms.label: transmembrane transport
terms.definition: The process in which a solute is transported across a lipid bilayer, from one side of a membrane to the other.

terms.label: chloride transmembrane transport
terms.definition: The process in which chloride is transported across a membrane.

terms.label: endomembrane system
terms.definition: A collection of membranous structures involved in transport within the cell. The main components of the endomembrane system are endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi bodies, vesicles, cell membrane and nuclear envelope. Members of the endomembrane system pass materials through each other or though the use of vesicles.

terms.label: adenyl nucleotide binding
terms.definition: Binding to an adenyl nucleotide, an adenosine esterified with (ortho)phosphate.

terms.label: AMP binding
terms.definition: Binding to AMP, adenosine monophosphate.

terms.label: adenyl ribonucleotide binding
terms.definition: Binding to an adenyl ribonucleotide, any compound consisting of adenosine esterified with (ortho)phosphate or an oligophosphate at any hydroxyl group on the ribose moiety.

terms.label: kinesin binding
terms.definition: Interacting selectively and non-covalently and stoichiometrically with kinesin, a member of a superfamily of microtubule-based motor proteins that perform force-generating tasks such as organelle transport and chromosome segregation.

ontology.scope: One NEW molecular function GO:0032559 represents measured ATP/ADP/AMP recognition. Typed ancestry and descendants show no overlap with the 33 seeded terms; no nested individual nucleotide term, ATPase, or new biological process is proposed. Transport and kinesin-binding refinements preserve their original source objects.

products.scope: Product order is preserved: name 1 is displayed P51795-2 (816 residues); name 2 is P51795-1 (746 residues). Official FASTAs confirm the latter equals displayed residues 71–816. The follow-up below resolves historical construct mapping while retaining distinct reported boundaries.

followup_4686.scope: Finite response to review 5482106836 and comment 6106003338; original source data retained.

product_mapping.boundary_scope: The native deposited sequence starts at displayed641. 2J9L labels the N-terminal M and eight C-terminal residues as expression tags; 2JA3 CIF similarly separates native residues571–746 from its own entry sequence. UniProt640–816 is retained as the curated crystallography range, not called rounding of638–816. This resolves domain correspondence, not a full-length assay of both natural products.

acidification.performed_step: Human ClC-5-dependent proton transport in HEK293 endosomes, with localized pore mutants and V-ATPase inhibition controls.
acidification.context: Not a universal native renal flux-direction claim; PMID:20430975 mouse bulk ATP-driven acidification remains separately described.

membrane_source.scope: Bulk membrane fraction and human developmental staining retain the original membrane term; no source-specific endosome replacement.
